items.summary:
Observable Discrepancy vulnerability in Drupal CAPTCHA for Drupal 7 allows unauthenticated attackers to test login credentials despite CAPTCHA protection.

When CAPTCHA is enabled on Drupal login forms, normal form validation can still run after a missing or incorrect CAPTCHA response. This may expose credential validation feedback and allow an attacker to distinguish invalid credentials from valid credentials paired with a failed CAPTCHA.



This issue affects CAPTCHA for Drupal 7: from 7.x-1.0 through 7.x-1.7.
items.title: CAPTCHA for Drupal 7 exposes login validation feedback after failed CAPTCHA

items.summary: probe-image-size 7.4.0 contains a regular expression denial of service vulnerability in lib/common/svg_header.js that allows remote unauthenticated attackers to block the event loop via crafted SVG doctypes. Attackers can supply SVGs with an unclosed internal subset followed by many ']' characters to trigger quadratic backtracking in probe.sync, probe(stream) or probe(url), causing repeated event loop stalls.
items.title: probe-image-size 7.4.0 ReDoS via SVG Doctype Prolog Parser

items.summary: probe-image-size before 7.5.0 contains an algorithmic-complexity denial of service vulnerability in lib/exif_utils.js that allows remote unauthenticated attackers to exhaust CPU by supplying self-referencing EXIF IFDs. Attackers can submit a crafted 9.6 KB JPEG with repeated ExifIFD and InteropIFD pointers to block the Node.js event loop for about 23 seconds.
items.title: probe-image-size before 7.5.0 Denial of Service via EXIF Sub-IFD Traversal

items.summary: probe-image-size before 7.5.0 contains an unbounded memory allocation vulnerability in lib/parse_stream/avif.js that allows remote attackers to exhaust memory via attacker-declared ftyp or meta box sizes. Attackers can supply an AVIF stream or URL to probe(url) or probe(stream) declaring a huge box length, forcing the parser to buffer all received bytes and causing denial of service.
items.title: probe-image-size before 7.5.0 Memory Exhaustion via AVIF Box Size

items.summary: probe-image-size before 7.5.0 contains an unbounded memory buffering vulnerability in parseExif in lib/parse_stream/webp.js that allows remote attackers to exhaust memory via an attacker-declared EXIF chunk length. Attackers can supply a WebP stream or URL to probe(url) or probe(stream) declaring a huge EXIF length after VP8X, causing unbounded buffering and process memory exhaustion.
items.title: probe-image-size before 7.5.0 Memory Exhaustion via WebP EXIF Chunk Length

items.summary: devpi-web before 5.2.0 contains an unauthenticated path traversal vulnerability in the +doc documentation route because docs_file_exists and docs_file_path in doczip.py never confine relpath to the documentation directory. Attackers can request a relpath with a leading // or percent-encoded .. segments to read server files, including the keyfs sqlite database holding password hashes.
items.title: devpi-web before 5.2.0 Unauthenticated Path Traversal via +doc Route

items.summary: devpi-server before 6.21.0 contains a path traversal vulnerability that allows authenticated users to write files outside the +files storage root by naming a user and index '..'. Attackers can self-register a '..' user, create a '..' index, and upload release files with attacker-chosen filenames and contents into a parent of the server directory.
items.title: devpi-server before 6.21.0 Path Traversal via '..' User and Index Names

items.summary: Qwik City before 1.20.3 (@builder.io/qwik-city) and @qwik.dev/router before 2.0.0-rc.4 contain an improperly controlled object modification vulnerability in formToObj that allows unauthenticated attackers to overwrite built-in function properties. Attackers can send a form POST with nested field names traversing inherited members of string values, breaking Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call process-wide until server restart.
items.title: Qwik City before 1.20.3 and Router before 2.0.0-rc.4 DoS via formToObj

items.summary: Cesanta Mongoose 7.22 before 7.24 with the built-in TLS stack contains an out-of-bounds read in mg_timegm() that allows remote attackers to crash the process via crafted X.509 certificate validity months. Attackers can present a certificate with month '00' or out-of-range values during the handshake, before signature verification, causing an unchecked dm array index and denial of service.
items.title: Cesanta Mongoose 7.22 before 7.24 Out-of-Bounds Read via mg_timegm

items.summary: Cesanta Mongoose 7.21 before 7.24 contains an out-of-bounds read vulnerability in rx_ip6() checksum validation that allows remote unauthenticated attackers to read past received packets by sending IPv6 extension headers. Attackers can send a single IPv6 TCP or ICMPv6 packet with extension headers, causing tcp6csum_ok() and icmp6csum_ok() to use the full payload length and read adjacent receive-buffer memory.
items.title: Cesanta Mongoose 7.21 before 7.24 Out-of-Bounds Read via IPv6 Checksum Validation

items.summary: audio-separator before 0.47.2 contains an insecure deserialization vulnerability that allows attackers to execute code by supplying malicious Demucs .th model files loaded via torch.load with weights_only=False. Local users writing to the shared /tmp/audio-separator-models/ default directory, or attackers controlling unverified model download sources, can execute code when victims run Demucs separation.
items.title: audio-separator before 0.47.2 RCE via Unsafe Pickle Deserialization of Demucs Models

items.summary: A flaw has been found in highlight highlight.js up to 11.12.0. The affected element is the function hljs.highlight of the file src/languages/livescript.js of the component Language Grammar Handler. Executing a manipulation of the argument text can lead to inefficient regular expression complexity. The attack can be launched remotely. The exploit has been published and may be used. The pull request to fix this issue awaits acceptance.
items.title: highlight highlight.js Language Grammar livescript.js hljs.highlight redos

items.summary: OceanWP WordPress Theme before 4.2.9 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability in the oceanwp_edd_terms_list() function in inc/edd/edd-helpers.php, which allows authenticated users with EDD download category creation permissions to inject malicious JavaScript by crafting a category name that breaks out of an unescaped HTML title attribute. Attackers can create a category name containing an event-handler payload that executes in the browser of visitors who interact with the category link on the public EDD archive page, potentially compromising an administrator's session if they view the affected page while authenticated.
items.title: OceanWP before 4.2.9 Stored XSS via EDD Category Name

items.summary: A vulnerability has been found in hankcs HanLP up to 2.1.6. The affected element is the function RNNLanguageModel.load_language_model of the file hanlp/layers/embeddings/contextual_string_embedding.py. Such manipulation of the argument model_file leads to deserialization. The attack may be performed from remote. The exploit has been disclosed to the public and may be used. Upgrading to version 2.1.7 is sufficient to fix this issue. The name of the patch is 6962907e37dfa467fa6dee164b5b1d0a904b24db. The affected component should be upgraded.
items.title: hankcs HanLP contextual_string_embedding.py RNNLanguageModel.load_language_model deserialization

items.summary: A flaw has been found in hankcs HanLP up to 2.1.6. Impacted is the function uncompress of the file hanlp/utils/io_util.py of the component TAR Archive Extraction Handler. This manipulation causes path traversal. The attack is possible to be carried out remotely. The exploit has been published and may be used. Upgrading to version 2.1.7 is recommended to address this issue. Patch name: feb0f82d12762cf4e687b9926efd90c672857780. You should upgrade the affected component.
items.title: hankcs HanLP TAR Archive Extraction io_util.py uncompress path traversal

items.summary: LibreChat is an enhanced ChatGPT clone that supports multiple AI providers. Prior to 0.8.6, POST /api/messages/:conversationId authorizes req.params.conversationId in api/server/middleware/validateMessageReq.js but persists attacker-controlled req.body.conversationId through api/server/routes/messages.js. An authenticated attacker can use an owned conversation in the URL while naming a victim conversation in the body, causing an attacker-controlled message to be stored in the victim conversation. This issue is fixed in version 0.8.6.
items.title: LibreChat: Cross-User Message Injection via Parameter Confusion

items.summary: LibreChat is an enhanced ChatGPT clone that supports multiple AI providers. Prior to 0.8.9, GET /api/permissions/search-principals passes the q parameter to JavaScript RegExp construction and MongoDB regex queries in packages/data-schemas/src/methods/userGroup.ts findGroupsByNamePattern and searchPrincipals without escaping metacharacters. An authenticated user with people-picker permission can submit a catastrophic-backtracking pattern that blocks the Node.js event loop and makes the service unresponsive to concurrent users; invalid patterns can also produce server errors. This issue is fixed in version 0.8.9.
items.title: LibreChat: Server-Side ReDoS via Unescaped Regex in Principal Search

items.summary: LibreChat is an enhanced ChatGPT clone that supports multiple AI providers. Prior to 0.8.8, packages/api/src/mcp/oauth/handler.ts createOAuthFetch validates only the initial destination for MCP OAuth discovery, registration, token, refresh, and revocation requests, then uses redirect-following fetch behavior without validating each redirect target. An attacker who can initiate MCP OAuth against a controlled endpoint can redirect server requests to internal or private addresses, reaching services that the initial SSRF checks should block. The separate MCP transport path already validates redirects and is not affected. This issue is fixed in version 0.8.8.
items.title: LibreChat: MCP OAuth requests can follow redirects to internal URLs after SSRF validation

items.summary: LibreChat is an enhanced ChatGPT clone that supports multiple AI providers. Prior to 0.8.7, POST /api/agents/actions/:agent_id in api/server/routes/agents/actions.js loads an existing action with owner credentials and merges editor-controlled metadata.domain and metadata.raw_spec while preserving metadata.api_key and related OAuth client secrets. A collaborator with EDIT permission can repoint an action to an attacker-controlled host, and a later tool invocation decrypts and sends the retained owner credential to that destination. This issue is fixed in version 0.8.7.
items.title: LibreChat: Shared-Agent Editor Can Exfiltrate Owner Action API Keys via OpenAPI Spec Swap

items.summary: LibreChat is an enhanced ChatGPT clone that supports multiple AI providers. Prior to 0.8.7, unauthenticated POST /api/user/verify requests in api/server/routes/user.js call api/server/services/AuthService.js verifyEmail and return distinct responses for unknown, verified, and unverified email addresses and the route lacks request throttling. A remote attacker can submit candidate addresses with invalid tokens to enumerate registered accounts and verification state, supporting targeted phishing or credential attacks. This issue is fixed in version 0.8.7.
items.title: LibreChat: Unauthenticated User Enumeration via Email Verification Endpoint

items.summary: LibreChat is an enhanced ChatGPT clone that supports multiple AI providers. Prior to 0.8.7, POST /api/auth/requestPasswordReset calls deleteTokens by user ID before creating a reset token, while password-reset and email-verification records in packages/data-schemas/src/methods/token.ts have no populated flow type. When password reset is enabled and email verification is enforced, an unauthenticated attacker who knows a target email can repeatedly delete pending verification tokens and prevent account verification until the unverified account expires. This issue is fixed in version 0.8.7.
items.title: LibreChat: Password Reset Can Wipe Email-Verification Tokens When Verification Is Enforced

items.summary: LibreChat is an enhanced ChatGPT clone that supports multiple AI providers. Prior to 0.8.7, POST /api/auth/2fa/verify-temp in api/server/routes/auth.js calls verify2FAWithTempToken and accepts repeated TOTP or backup-code guesses without a dedicated attempt limiter. An attacker must first possess valid primary credentials and a valid five-minute temp token, but can then make repeated second-factor attempts and obtain a full session if a valid code is guessed. This issue is fixed in version 0.8.7.
items.title: LibreChat: Missing Rate Limiting on 2FA Verification Endpoint Allows TOTP Guessing Attempts

items.summary: LibreChat is an enhanced ChatGPT clone that supports multiple AI providers. From 0.8.5 until 0.8.6, GET /api/user in api/server/controllers/UserController.js getUserController serializes federatedTokens and tokenset to the authenticated browser because an earlier response-sanitization fix was not applied to this endpoint. Browser-context script can obtain OAuth access, ID, and refresh credentials that were intended to remain server-side. This issue is fixed in version 0.8.6.
items.title: LibreChat: Federated OAuth Tokens Exposed via `/api/user` Endpoint

items.summary: LibreChat is an enhanced ChatGPT clone that supports multiple AI providers. Prior to 0.8.7, packages/data-schemas/src/methods/file.ts updateFileUsage accepts chat attachment files[].file_id values without restricting the lookup to the authenticated owner. An authenticated attacker who obtains another user's file identifier, including through GET /api/share/{shareId} for a shared conversation, can attach that file to a chat, causing extracted document text to enter the model context. The same operation can remove expiration metadata from the victim file. This issue is fixed in version 0.8.7.
items.title: LibreChat: Unauthorized File Content Access via Chat Attachment file_id

items.summary: LibreChat is an enhanced ChatGPT clone that supports multiple AI providers. Prior to 0.8.6, client/src/components/Chat/Input/MCPConfigDialog.tsx renders the remote MCP details.description value through dangerouslySetInnerHTML without sanitization, allowing a malicious MCP server to execute script when a user opens the configuration dialog. The secondary client/src/components/Banners/Banner.tsx sink similarly renders administrator-controlled banner.message HTML without sanitization for all users. Script execution occurs in the LibreChat browser origin and can expose browser-context data or alter displayed content. This issue is fixed in version 0.8.6.
items.title: LibreChat: Remote MCP Server Description XSS via Unsanitized dangerouslySetInnerHTML; secondary Admin Banner sink lacks DOMPurify

items.summary: LibreChat is an enhanced ChatGPT clone that supports multiple AI providers. From 0.7.0 until 0.8.6, when local registration is enabled and at least one social provider is configured, POST /api/auth/register passes an unparsed request object into api/server/services/AuthService.js, allowing an unauthenticated attacker to persist a forged provider value for a known victim email. The api/strategies/socialLogin.js email-fallback path then accepts the planted record when the victim signs in because it compares the stored provider name without requiring the provider subject identifier. The victim OAuth session and the attacker local-password session become bound to the same user record, giving the attacker persistent read and write access to data created by the victim. The first-user administrator role is an additional conditional impact only on a fresh deployment. This issue is fixed in version 0.8.6.
items.title: LibreChat: Pre-registration account takeover via attacker-controlled `provider` field and social-login email fallback

items.summary: LibreChat is an enhanced ChatGPT clone that supports multiple AI providers. Prior to 0.8.6, the POST /api/auth/login local-login validation path in api/strategies/localStrategy.js logs req.body, including the submitted plaintext password, during a Zod validation failure. The standard browser form validation makes this path less likely through the normal interface, but a direct invalid login request can reach it, and the logging formatter does not redact the password stored in metadata. A principal with access to application stdout, error logs, or journal output can recover the submitted credential. This issue is fixed in version 0.8.6.
items.title: LibreChat: Plaintext password logged on login validation error

items.summary: codebase-memory-mcp provides local code intelligence for developers and AI agents through a persistent graph and MCP tools. Prior to 0.10.0, the indexer's .gitignore matcher implemented * and ** through recursive backtracking without a work bound. A repository containing a pattern with repeated wildcard groups and a long path could make matching work grow exponentially, allowing a single ignore rule to stall discovery indefinitely and, before worker isolation, stall the server. The impact is limited to availability, and the bounded matcher does not claim that every expensive input is eliminated. This issue is fixed in version 0.10.0.
items.title: codebase-memory-mcp: Catastrophic backtracking in .gitignore glob matching lets a repository stall the indexer

items.summary: codebase-memory-mcp provides local code intelligence for developers and AI agents through a persistent graph and MCP tools. Prior to 0.9.0, automatic import of a repository's .codebase-memory/ artifact allocated a decompression buffer using the attacker-controlled 64-bit original_size value from artifact.json but truncated that value to int when passing the destination capacity to the Zstandard decompressor. A value with bit 31 set became negative and was sign-extended to a large size_t, allowing the decompressor to write frame content beyond the actual allocation. Indexing a malicious repository containing the crafted artifact could corrupt heap memory with attacker-controlled bytes, causing a reliable crash and potentially code execution. This issue is fixed in version 0.9.0.
items.title: codebase-memory-mcp: Heap buffer overflow on artifact import via int-truncated decompression capacity

items.summary: codebase-memory-mcp provides local code intelligence for developers and AI agents through a persistent graph and MCP tools. Prior to 0.9.0, the Cypher parser accepted an unbounded number of projection items in RETURN and WITH clauses while projection executors indexed fixed 32-element stack arrays using the parsed count. A query_graph query with more than 32 projection items could therefore write beyond those arrays, and a related result-column path could read uninitialized stack slots even when no node matched. Any caller of query_graph, including an agent whose query is influenced by untrusted content, could cause a reliable server crash and potentially compromise process confidentiality and integrity. This issue is fixed in version 0.9.0.
items.title: codebase-memory-mcp: Stack out-of-bounds write in query_graph via a RETURN or WITH clause with more than 32 items

items.summary: codebase-memory-mcp provides local code intelligence for developers and AI agents through a persistent graph and MCP tools. Prior to 0.9.0, the detect_changes tool validated the base_branch argument for shell metacharacters but omitted the leading-dash check before placing the value in the revision position of a git diff command. Git therefore interpreted an option-shaped base_branch value, including --output, as a command option instead of a revision, allowing a caller to create or overwrite a caller-chosen file with Git diff output under the server process's permissions. Arbitrary code execution was not demonstrated. This issue is fixed in version 0.9.0.
items.title: codebase-memory-mcp: git option injection through base_branch in detect_changes allows writing a file outside the project

items.summary: codebase-memory-mcp provides local code intelligence for developers and AI agents through a persistent graph and MCP tools. Prior to 0.9.1-rc.1, the optional graph UI's POST /api/process-kill route omitted the indexing-job ownership check on Windows while retaining that check on POSIX systems. A requester able to reach the optional UI could supply an arbitrary process identifier, causing TerminateProcess to stop any process that the server user was permitted to terminate. The flaw affects the Windows-specific process termination path and can cause a high availability impact without disclosing or modifying data. This issue is fixed in version 0.9.1-rc.1.
items.title: codebase-memory-mcp: UI process-kill route skipped the ownership check on Windows, allowing termination of arbitrary processes

items.summary: MaxKB is an open-source AI assistant for enterprise. Prior to 2.10.7-lts, custom Tool Init Param definitions accept attacker-controlled props_info.rules[].validator strings through POST /admin/api/workspace/{workspace_id}/tool and PUT /admin/api/workspace/{workspace_id}/tool/{tool_id}, store them without restriction, and pass them to eval() when the parameter form renders. An authenticated user with the default USER workspace role can store JavaScript and trigger execution by opening the tool's Debug screen before entering or submitting a parameter value. The same Init Param form is exposed to accounts with edit permission on the tool, but execution by a different account was not independently verified. The confirmed script runs in the MaxKB origin; access to another user's bearer token and authenticated account authority is plausible only if that user renders the malicious form. This issue is fixed in version 2.10.7-lts.
items.title: MaxKB: Eval Injection via Custom Tool "Init Param" Validator Rule Allows Arbitrary JavaScript Execution

items.summary: RabbitMQ is a messaging and streaming broker. In the affected revision identified by the advisory, the AMQP 1.0 server_mode parser in deps/amqp10_common/src/amqp10_binary_parser.erl stops at the first body section and preserves the remaining bytes in bare_and_footer without validating message-section order. An authenticated publisher with write permission can place a properties section carrying a forged user-id after the body, causing rabbit_access_control:check_user_id/2 to see no user-id while permissive downstream AMQP 1.0 decoders or AMQP 0-9-1 conversion through classic and quorum queues expose the forged identity. Applications that rely on RabbitMQ-validated user-id metadata can therefore accept attacker-controlled publisher attribution. Strict consumers that reject out-of-order sections are not vulnerable to identity spoofing, and the issue does not bypass broker routing or destination authorization. This issue is fixed in version 4.3.5.
items.title: RabbitMQ: AMQP 1.0 post-body properties bypass user-ID validation and reach consumers

items.summary: MapServer is a system for developing web-based GIS applications. Prior to 8.6.5, MapServer's PostgreSQL JOIN implementation in src/mappostgresql.c copies the source layer attribute selected by JOIN FROM into joininfo->from_value and embeds it without parameterization or escaping into a dynamically generated PostgreSQL query executed by PQexec(). When PostgreSQL JOIN support is enabled, an attacker who can control that source feature attribute can inject quote characters and SQL operators that alter the intended WHERE predicate. This second-order injection can cause unintended rows and JOIN attributes to be returned, potentially exposing information from unrelated PostgreSQL records. This issue is fixed in version 8.6.5.
items.title: MapServer: PostgreSQL JOIN second-order SQL injection in src/mappostgresql.c

items.summary: MapServer is a system for developing web-based GIS applications. From 6.0 until 8.6.5, MapServer's WMS OpenLayers output, selected by FORMAT=application/openlayers or template=openlayers, substitutes a request-derived online-resource value into a single-quoted JavaScript string in src/maptemplate.c. The prior remediation for GHSA-xqj6-vjqr-33vv used msEscapeJSonLikeString() to protect the JavaScript string but did not neutralize angle brackets, so attacker-controlled X-Forwarded-Host or X-Forwarded-Proto values can still terminate the script element at the HTML parser layer. Deployments that expose attacker-controlled PATH_INFO or map= values reaching the same string are also affected. An unauthenticated attacker can cause arbitrary JavaScript to execute in a victim's browser under the MapServer origin when the victim loads the crafted output. This issue is fixed in version 8.6.5.
items.title: MapServer: Reflected XSS in WMS OpenLayers output via the `X-Forwarded-Host` header

items.summary: MapServer is a system for developing web-based GIS applications. From 8.2.0 until 8.6.5, an unauthenticated attacker can send a WMS GetLegendGraphic request with a nonempty BBOX and repeated LAYER parameters to trigger a heap buffer overflow in msWMSDispatch() in src/mapwms.cpp. The handler appends synthesized entries to cgiRequestObj.ParamNames and cgiRequestObj.ParamValues at NumParams without retaining the arrays' capacity or reallocating them, while incrementing NumParams inside the loop. Once the parser's hidden capacity is exhausted, the writes pass the heap allocation boundary. A single request can corrupt heap memory and crash the process; code execution may be possible but was not demonstrated. This issue is fixed in version 8.6.5.
items.title: MapServer: Heap buffer overflow in WMS GetLegendGraphic via repeated LAYER parameters

items.summary: MapServer is a system for developing web-based GIS applications. Prior to 8.6.5, an unauthenticated reflected cross-site scripting vulnerability in OGC API Features collection-items HTML output allows crafted offset or limit query parameter values from raw CGI request handling in src/mapogcapi.cpp to reach template.params.offset or template.params.limit. share/ogcapi/templates/html-bootstrap/collection-items.html inserts those values without quoting or escaping into a script element. A victim who follows a crafted request can have the script element terminated by attacker-controlled markup, causing arbitrary JavaScript to execute under the MapServer origin and enabling access to browser-session data, actions as the victim, and content manipulation. This issue is fixed in 8.6.5.
items.title: MapServer Reflected XSS via unescaped offset/limit query params injected into <script> in OGC API Features HTML output

items.summary: MapServer is a system for developing web-based GIS applications. From 4.4.0 until 8.6.5, an unauthenticated remote attacker can send a WCS GetCoverage XML POST request whose BoundingBox element omits the crs attribute, causing xmlGetProp() in src/mapwcs.cpp to return null. msWCSParseRequest() then calls string functions on the null value before normal WCS exception handling, crashing the CGI or FastCGI worker. The analogous KVP or GET path is not affected because it obtains a count-validated, non-null token. A single request can terminate one worker, and repeated requests can exhaust a fixed worker pool and deny service. This issue is fixed in version 8.6.5.
items.title: MapServer: WCS POST: NULL-Dereference Denial of Service When `BoundingBox` Omits `crs`

items.summary: MapServer is a system for developing web-based GIS applications. Prior to 8.6.5, MapServer's MySQL JOIN implementation in src/mapjoin.c copies the source layer attribute selected by JOIN ... FROM into joininfo->target and inserts it into the query built by msMySQLJoinNext() without parameterization or SQL escaping. When MySQL JOIN support is enabled, an attacker who can control that source feature attribute, including through imported shapefile or DBF data or another untrusted spatial source, can inject SQL operators or expressions that change the intended JOIN predicate. This can bypass the intended key comparison and expose unrelated records from the MySQL or MariaDB JOIN table through output templates, query responses, or downstream application logic. This issue is fixed in version 8.6.5.
items.title: MapServer: MySQL JOIN second-order SQL injection in src/mapjoin.c

items.summary: NukeViet CMS is a multi Content Management System. From 4.5.08 until 4.5.12 and 4.6.02, an attacker can place NukeViet's internal {@[, ]@}, [@{, and }@] sanitizer markers in an iframe srcdoc value by encoding square brackets as HTML entities. Recursive NukeViet\Core\Request::filterTags() processing decodes the characters, accepts the forged marker, and later converts it to real markup without normal tag or attribute filtering. Because an unsandboxed srcdoc iframe shares the parent origin and iframe is enabled by default through NV_ALLOWED_HTML_TAGS, stored Contact messages, comments with the editor enabled, or submitted articles can execute JavaScript with the viewer's session. This issue is fixed in versions 4.5.12 and 4.6.02.
items.title: NukeViet CMS: Stored XSS via internal marker injection in iframe srcdoc sanitization

items.summary: NukeViet CMS is a multi Content Management System. Prior to 4.5.12 and 4.6.02, an attacker with access to an SVG upload flow can hide a script element in an internal DTD entity. NukeViet\Files\Upload::check_svg_tmpfile() loads the document without entity expansion, leaving a DOMEntityReference, and sanitize_svg_dom() inspects only element nodes, while browsers expand the entity when the stored file is served as image/svg+xml. The SVG path also returned before verify_image() and preserved the original bytes, so the hidden script reached disk unchanged. Guest comment attachments make the upload unauthenticated only when a module's comment feature is open to the All or Guest group and allowattachcomm is enabled; module administrators can also use the file manager, allowing same-origin script execution in an administrator's session. This issue is fixed in versions 4.5.12 and 4.6.02.
items.title: NukeViet CMS: Stored XSS via SVG upload: the sanitizer is blind to markup hidden inside an internal DTD entity

items.summary: NukeViet CMS is a multi Content Management System. From 4.5.00 until 4.5.13 and 4.6.02, an unauthenticated attacker can place a multiply encoded value in the news module search q parameter. $nv_Request->get_title() decodes and sanitizes the input once, but modules/news/funcs/search.php subsequently applies urldecode() after sanitization. The resulting raw keyword reaches the {KEY} search-input attribute through search_theme() and the no-results element through search_result_theme() in the default and mobile themes, permitting attribute or tag injection and same-origin JavaScript execution when a victim opens the crafted search URL. This issue is fixed in versions 4.5.13 and 4.6.02.
items.title: NukeViet CMS: Reflected XSS in news module search via double URL decoding of the q parameter

items.summary: NukeViet CMS is a multi Content Management System. Prior to 4.5.12 and 4.6.02, an attacker who can reach an image-upload flow can upload a valid image with appended PHP short-tag code and a double-extension filename. NukeViet\Files\Upload::save_file() relied on verify_image(), which missed the <? short-open tag, while filename handling preserved embedded dots, validation inspected only the final extension, and an .htaccess rule blocked PHP extensions only at the end of the URI. On Apache mod_php systems configured with short_open_tag and a PHP extension handler, the stored polyglot can execute as PHP and run operating-system commands as the web-server user; PHP-FPM, nginx, and end-anchored handler configurations are not exposed to the execution step. This issue is fixed in versions 4.5.12 and 4.6.02.
items.title: NukeViet CMS: Remote Code Execution via image-upload bypass chain (PHP short-tag detection bypass + double-extension filename)

items.summary: NukeViet CMS is a multi Content Management System. Prior to 4.6.01, an unauthenticated visitor can submit Contact module content containing numeric HTML entities with more than eight leading zeros in a URL-bearing attribute. NukeViet\Core\Request::unhtmlentities() does not decode that form before filterAttr() checks for a javascript: scheme, but browsers decode it when rendering the stored content. With an allowed tag such as the default iframe, the reconstructed script URL executes in the administration origin when staff view the message, permitting session-riding actions while remaining unable to read the HttpOnly session cookie directly. This issue is fixed in version 4.6.01.
items.title: NukeViet CMS: Unauthenticated Stored XSS in the Contact module via HTML sanitizer bypass

items.summary: NukeViet CMS is a multi Content Management System. From the 3.x release line until 4.6.01, an unauthenticated visitor can submit a Contact module message containing an event-handler attribute prefixed by a slash. NukeViet\Core\Request::filterTags() tokenizes attributes using only ASCII spaces, so it sees /onerror and misses the ^on denylist, while the browser treats the slash as a separator and activates onerror. The message is stored and rendered without output encoding in the administration panel, which lacks a Content Security Policy, allowing same-origin JavaScript execution when an administrator opens the message. This issue is fixed in version 4.6.01.
items.title: NukeViet CMS: Unauthenticated Stored XSS in the Contact module

items.summary: NukeViet CMS is a multi Content Management System. From 4.5.00 until 4.6.01, an authenticated settings-module administrator can upload a PKCS#12 S/MIME certificate whose X.509 Subject CN contains path separators and traversal components. The smimeadd handler in admin/settings/smtp.php applies only an at-sign replacement before using the CN in .key, .crt, and .pem paths beneath data/certs. Traversal can select attacker-chosen paths outside data/certs, but writes remain constrained to already-existing writable directories and the permitted extensions. Within that constraint, attacker-controlled PEM data can overwrite certificate assets, including a DKIM private key; when the curl.cainfo PHP directive is empty, the attacker can also replace cacert.pem and undermine outbound TLS verification. This issue is fixed in version 4.6.01.
items.title: NukeViet CMS: Authenticated path traversal to arbitrary file write via S/MIME certificate CN in SMTP settings

items.summary: NukeViet CMS is a multi Content Management System. In 4.6.00, an unauthenticated attacker can place the configured domain in X-Forwarded-Host while choosing a different destination in the ordinary Host header. The earlier fix validates only the forwarded value in includes/mainfile.php, while set_ini_file() in includes/ini.php constructs an outbound cURL request from the separately retained NV_SERVER_NAME before the ordinary host is rejected. Redirect following can carry the blind request to an attacker-selected private host, port, and path and invoke internal HTTP endpoints. This issue is fixed in version 4.6.01.
items.title: NukeViet: Pre-authentication SSRF via incomplete X-Forwarded-Host fix
