items.summary: NukeViet CMS is a multi Content Management System. Prior to 4.6.01, a super-administrator satisfying the NV_IS_SPADMIN gate can use modules/users/admin/fields.php to store an arbitrary existing PHP function in the func_callback setting for a custom profile field because the callback name is checked only with function_exists() and no allowlist restricts which function may be selected. modules/users/fields.check.php later invokes that function through call_user_func() when the field is validated through registration, profile editing, or administrator editing. Selecting a command-execution function crosses the super-administrator to operating-system boundary and executes commands as the web-server account, while ordinary users can trigger the stored callback after it is configured. Because the remediation validates callbacks only when they are written, upgrading does not remove a malicious callback already stored in the database, which must be cleaned manually. This issue is fixed in version 4.6.01.
items.title: NukeViet CMS: Remote Code Execution via unrestricted custom field validation callback in the `users` module

items.summary: NukeViet CMS is a multi Content Management System. In 4.6.00, an unauthenticated attacker can rotate X-Forwarded-For because vendor/vinades/nukeviet/Core/Ips.php accepts forwarded client-IP headers without first confirming that REMOTE_ADDR is a trusted proxy. The resulting NV_CLIENT_IP keys the administrator login blocker in includes/core/admin_login.php; changing only the header value bypasses that lockout and permits effectively unlimited password guesses. The same spoofable address is also consumed by the user login blocker in modules/users/funcs/login.php, IP restrictions, bans, flood controls, and security logs, but those additional code-level effects were not dynamically demonstrated. This issue is fixed in version 4.6.01.
items.title: NukeVie: Login Lockout Bypass via Untrusted Forwarded-IP Headers

items.summary: NukeViet CMS is a multi Content Management System. Prior to 4.6.00, a network attacker who can alter outbound traffic to the extension store can exploit the HTTP client's disabled sslverify setting to substitute a serialized response. Extension-store handlers pass the response to unserialize() without an allowed_classes restriction, allowing an in-tree GuzzleHttp\Cookie\FileCookieJar gadget to write attacker-controlled content to a chosen path. When a GODADMIN opens or uses the store list, detail, install, or update functions, the substituted response can write a PHP file under the web root and execute code as the web-server user. This issue is fixed in version 4.6.00.
items.title: NukeViet CMS: PHP Object Injection to RCE in extension store via unverified HTTP response

items.summary: NukeViet CMS is a multi Content Management System. Prior to 4.5.09, a user with news-posting permission can bypass NukeViet\Core\Request::filterAttr() by prefixing an event-handler attribute with an ASCII form-feed character, which PHP trimming preserves but browsers treat as whitespace. NukeViet\Core\Request::unhtmlentities() omitted a decimal HTML entity tab embedded in a javascript: URI. These parser differences allow persistent event handlers or script URLs to survive filtering in vendor/vinades/nukeviet/Core/Request.php and execute for visitors, including administrators. This issue is fixed in version 4.5.09.
items.title: NukeViet CMS: Multiple Anti-XSS Filter Bypasses Leading to Stored XSS in News Module

items.summary: NukeViet CMS is a multi Content Management System. Prior to 4.5.09, an authenticated administrator can submit a crafted attach value to modules/comment/admin/edit.php. The handler removed a fixed-length upload prefix without validating containment, allowing padding followed by a traversal path to be stored in the database. When the comment is deleted, modules/comment/admin/del.php joins the stored path to NV_UPLOADS_REAL_DIR and passes it to nv_deletefile(), whose realpath() check restricts deletion only to NV_ROOTDIR rather than the upload directory, permitting deletion of application files such as config.php and causing an outage. This issue is fixed in version 4.5.09.
items.title: NukeViet CMS: Path Traversal to Arbitrary File Deletion in Edit Comment Function

items.summary: NukeViet CMS is a multi Content Management System. Prior to 4.5.09, the Comment module accepts attacker-controlled base64 content in the status_comment parameter through modules/comment/funcs/main.php; modules/comment/comment.php decodes it with nv_base64_decode() and assigns it to STATUS_COMMENT without output escaping. The required checkss token was derived from the site-wide NV_CACHE_PREFIX rather than NV_CHECK_SESSION, so a token disclosed in public comment markup could be reused across sessions in a crafted URL. An unauthenticated attacker can therefore cause decoded HTML or JavaScript to render in a victim's browser and perform phishing or same-origin actions. This issue is fixed in version 4.5.09.
items.title: NukeViet CMS: Unauthenticated Reflected XSS in Comment Module

items.summary: NukeViet CMS is a multi Content Management System. From the 4.x release line until 4.5.09, a low-privileged authenticated user can store script-breaking content in the first_name and last_name profile fields used to form a comment display name. Both reply links in themes/default/modules/comment/comment.tpl interpolate {COMMENT.post_name} into the inline onclick call to nv_commment_feedback(). HTML numeric references produced by Request::_get_title() are decoded by the browser before JavaScript parsing, so clicking Reply can terminate the string and execute attacker-controlled JavaScript in the visitor's origin, including an administrator's session. This issue is fixed in version 4.5.09.
items.title: NukeViet: stored XSS through comment reply display names

items.summary: NukeViet CMS is a multi Content Management System. Prior to 4.5.09, an unauthenticated attacker can submit the __serverInfoUpdate=1 field while controlling X-Forwarded-Host and X-Forwarded-Proto. NukeViet\Core\Server::standardizeHost() did not validate the forwarded host against my_domains, and a trailing slash could preserve an attacker-selected port that server_info_update() used to construct a cURL request in includes/ini.php before authentication. The blind, HEAD-only request uses a fixed path, but it permits internal host and port discovery and can poison cached server_headers. This issue is fixed in version 4.5.09.
items.title: NukeViet CMS: Pre-authentication SSRF via X-Forwarded-Host in NukeViet

items.summary: monailabel (aka MONAI Label) through 0.8.5 allows directory traversal, with resultant remote code execution, via the image parameter to the PUT /datastore/image endpoint, as exploited in the wild starting in September 2026.
items.title: CVE-2026-133968

items.summary: Pozeiden is a MermaidJS renderer written in Zig. Prior to 0.3.0, Pozeiden emits attacker-controlled Mermaid values into SVG attributes or markup without sufficient XML escaping or URL scheme validation, and first-party consumers such as zigmark and policypress embed the generated SVG raw into HTML. The click href syntax can introduce a dangerous URL scheme or break out of an attribute; style, classDef, ::: class assignment, and linkStyle color values can inject fill or stroke markup; color and font-weight values can escape text attributes; %%{init}%% themeVariables can inject global renderer attributes; and quadrant y-axis labels can introduce raw markup. These paths involve src/svg/writer.zig, src/renderers/flowchart.zig, src/renderers/quadrant.zig, and src/root.zig. An attacker who can influence rendered Mermaid source can therefore store script-bearing SVG that executes when another user views the published HTML. This issue is fixed in version 0.3.0.
items.title: Pozeiden: SVG output injection (stored XSS) via click href, style/classDef colors, %%{init}%% theme variables, and quadrant labels

items.summary: Pozeiden is a MermaidJS renderer written in Zig. Prior to 0.3.0, src/renderers/c4.zig, src/renderers/class.zig, src/renderers/er.zig, and src/renderers/requirement.zig use fixed row-layout arrays while deriving subsequent loop bounds from an untrusted diagram's actual item count, and src/renderers/state.zig indexes a fixed depth array using user-controlled nesting depth. A valid diagram with at least 193 grid items can make the row count exceed the 64-row storage, while a deeply nested state diagram can exceed the col_count depth storage through the public pozeiden.render() path. Safe CLI and ReleaseSafe builds abort the rendering process, enabling reliable denial of service in applications that render untrusted diagrams. ReleaseSmall WASM builds with safety checks disabled instead perform out-of-bounds stack reads or writes, creating a memory-safety violation. This issue is fixed in version 0.3.0.
items.title: Pozeiden: Out-of-bounds read/write (crash / memory corruption) on valid diagrams in grid-layout renderers

items.summary: mcp-ssh-manager is an MCP server for managing servers over SSH with human approval, an encrypted vault, and a live audit trail. Prior to 3.8.5, ssh_backup_create, ssh_backup_restore, ssh_backup_schedule, and ssh_backup_list build remote shell commands from caller-controlled values in src/backup-manager.js and inline backup handlers in src/index.js without neutralizing shell metacharacters. Crafted database, connection, backup directory, path, exclusion, schedule, or comment arguments can therefore execute arbitrary OS commands on managed remote servers as the configured SSH user. ssh_backup_schedule can persist execution through cron. ssh_backup_list does not pass through the server policy check and remains available in readonly and restricted modes, allowing command execution despite those restrictions. Tool arguments can be supplied by a malicious or compromised MCP client or steered through indirect prompt injection; fully trusted benign arguments do not trigger the issue. The earlier database-helper remediation for CVE-2026-77383 applied shell quoting to src/database-manager.js but did not cover these parallel backup builders. This issue is fixed in version 3.8.5.
items.title: mcp-ssh-manager: Remote code execution (RCE) via command injection in the backup subsystem

items.summary: mcp-ssh-manager is an MCP server for managing servers over SSH with human approval, an encrypted vault, and a live audit trail. Prior to 3.6.7, ssh_db_list, ssh_db_dump, ssh_db_import, and ssh_db_restore in src/database-manager.js interpolate caller-controlled database, table, collection, file path, user, host, port, and password values into shell-evaluated command strings without neutralization. Shell metacharacters in these arguments therefore execute arbitrary commands on the configured SSH target as the account used by the MCP server. ssh_db_list is classified as read-only and remains available in readonly and restricted server security modes, so this path bypasses the command-execution boundary those modes are intended to enforce. The dump and import builders are blocked in readonly mode but remain vulnerable in the default unrestricted mode. The earlier version 3.6.5 hardening covered only ssh_db_query query text; it did not protect the list, dump, import, or restore builders, or the connection flags used by query builders. This issue is fixed in version 3.6.7.
items.title: mcp-ssh-manager: Command injection in mcp-ssh-manager database helpers (ssh_db_list / ssh_db_dump / ssh_db_import)

items.summary: isomorphic-git is a pure JavaScript implementation of Git for Node.js and browsers. Prior to 1.38.8, git cherry-pick applies tree changes through applyTreeChanges in src/utils/walkerToTreeEntryMap.js without checking whether a leading path component is a symbolic link. If a victim worktree contains a tracked symlink to a location outside the worktree and a cherry-picked tree places a file beneath that path, the write follows the symlink and materializes attacker-controlled blob content at the external destination. This allows arbitrary file writes and can cause data tampering, code injection into interpreted files, privilege escalation, denial of service, or follow-on code execution depending on the selected target path. This issue is fixed in version 1.38.8.
items.title: isomorphic-git: Arbitrary File Write via Symlink

items.summary: isomorphic-git is a pure JavaScript implementation of Git for Node.js and browsers. Prior to 1.38.7, tree-entry validation in src/models/GitTree.js does not reject the Windows NTFS reserved pathname alias .git::$INDEX_ALLOCATION. When clone() or checkout materializes an attacker-controlled tree containing this alias on Windows using an NTFS filesystem, the alias resolves to the active .git directory and permits writes to trusted repository metadata instead of a normal worktree directory. A malicious repository or object stream can therefore poison repository configuration, hooks, refs, attributes, or other gitdir state. Strict hosting that rejects hasDotgit objects can block the crafted tree, and non-NTFS systems do not interpret the pathname as the active gitdir. isomorphic-git performs the gitdir write but does not itself execute the written hook or configuration; a later native Git or compatible-tool action, such as processing a poisoned core.fsmonitor value, can execute configured commands as the victim developer or CI identity. This issue is fixed in version 1.38.7.
items.title: isomorphic-git: NTFS .git::$INDEX_ALLOCATION alias bypass writes into the active gitdir

items.summary: Avahi is a system which facilitates service discovery on a local network via the mDNS/DNS-SD protocol suite. In 0.9-rc4 and earlier on NetBSD architectures such as x86_64 where char is signed and the ctype guard-page change is present, avahi_domain_hash can pass a negative value to tolower when a resource-record name contains a byte at or above 128. The invalid ctype input reliably raises SIGSEGV, allowing a remote peer on the local network to crash the Avahi daemon. This issue is fixed with 0.9-rc5.
items.title: avahi-daemon crashes on receiving resource records where names contain bytes >= 128 (on NetBSD)

items.summary: pmo-platform is a modular PMO and release-management platform for Claude Code. Prior to 3.73, release/skills/pmo-skill-refiner/eval-viewer/generate_review.py and viewer.html contain three security weaknesses in the local evaluation viewer. During workspace scanning and generation, _find_runs_recursive and build_run follow symlinks and embed_file reads their targets without confining resolved paths to the workspace, although the server do_GET path is not a traversal surface. embed_file also reads output files without a size cap or redaction, allowing secrets or personally identifiable information to be embedded in a no-auth locally served page or shareable static file. Separately, do_POST /api/feedback writes caller-supplied JSON without authentication, an Origin check, or a cross-site request forgery token, allowing a malicious page or DNS-rebound localhost target to modify feedback while the server runs. This issue is fixed in version 3.73.
items.title: pmo-platform: eval-viewer (pmo-skill-refiner): symlink-following arbitrary file read, verbatim secret/PII embedding, and CSRF write on the local review server

items.summary: pmo-platform is a modular PMO and release-management platform for Claude Code. Prior to 3.73, core/hooks/block-fragile-refs.sh and core/hooks/block-gh-path-leak.sh source co-shipped awk primitives from core/hooks/lib/ and degrade when a required primitive is absent. In a partial or corrupted deployment, block-gh-path-leak.sh skips its entire path-leak check, while block-fragile-refs.sh skips only the positional-issue-reference detector and continues running its other detectors. Both hooks operate in a warning posture, so the impact is a skipped warning rather than bypass of an enforcing control, with no established exfiltration or code-execution primitive. This issue is fixed in version 3.73.
items.title: pmo-platform: Warn-mode security hooks fail open (skip their check) when a co-shipped awk primitive is absent

items.summary:
The IPv6 neighbour discovery code in subsys/net/ip/ipv6_nbr.c keeps packets that are waiting for address resolution on a per-neighbour pending queue. A queued packet holds two references: the one handed over by the sender and a second one taken by net_ipv6_send_ns() when the packet is put on the queue. The Router Advertisement handler handle_ra_input() popped each packet off the queue and passed it to net_send_data(), relying on a trailing nbr_clear_ns_pending() call to release the queue reference — but that call then found the queue already empty and released nothing, so one reference was leaked for every pending packet flushed on an RA.

Router Advertisements are unauthenticated link-local ICMPv6 messages, so any node on the same link can trigger the flush. An attacker can make the leak deterministic by advertising itself as a router without a source link-layer address option, so the victim's neighbour entry stays INCOMPLETE, then inducing the victim to transmit through that next hop (the packet is queued and a neighbour solicitation is sent), leaving the solicitation unanswered and sending a further RA to drain the queue. Each round leaks one struct net_pkt together with its net_buf chain.

Leaked packets are never returned to the fixed-size pools, so the loss is permanent for the lifetime of the boot. With CONFIG_NET_PKT_TX_COUNT defaulting to 4 (14 with CONFIG_NET_PKT_LARGE_DEFAULTS), a small number of repetitions exhausts the transmit packet slab and the node stops being able to send any traffic. The impact is availability only: the reference count is always too high, never too low, so no use-after-free or memory corruption arises.

The fix moves the flush into a helper, nbr_send_pending(), which releases the queue reference for every packet it takes off the queue before handing the remaining reference to net_send_data(), and releases that one too if the send is refused.
items.title: Network packet reference leak in IPv6 Router Advertisement handling leads to buffer pool exhaustion

items.summary:
The SMSC911x/LAN9220 Ethernet driver stages every outgoing frame in a fixed-size static buffer before pushing it to the controller FIFO. eth_tx() in drivers/ethernet/eth_smsc911x.c took the frame length from net_pkt_get_len(pkt) and passed it directly to net_pkt_read(pkt, tx_buf, total_len), with no comparison against the size of tx_buf (NET_ETH_MAX_FRAME_SIZE). net_pkt_read() takes no destination size and only fails when the packet is shorter than the requested length, so any packet longer than the staging buffer was copied past its end.

Nothing between the IP layer and the driver bounds the frame to what the link can carry: ethernet_send() in subsys/net/l2/ethernet/ethernet.c performs no length check, and the IPv6 output path only compares the packet against the interface MTU when CONFIG_NET_IPV6_FRAGMENT is enabled (it is disabled by default). The size the stack will build is therefore governed by the interface MTU, and that MTU is remotely settable: handle_ra_input() in subsys/net/ip/ipv6_nbr.c honours the MTU option of any Router Advertisement with a value up to 0xffff, gated only by the standard hop-limit-255 and link-local-source checks. An unauthenticated attacker on the same link can raise the MTU and then have the device emit a single frame of several kilobytes, for example as a TCP segment from any service that returns more than ~1.5 KB or as an oversized UDP datagram.

The result is an out-of-bounds write into .bss immediately after tx_buf, with the overrun length and much of its content derived from the transmitted frame. Consequences range from corruption of adjacent kernel data and a crash to potential control-flow influence where the clobbered globals hold pointers; the practical overrun size is bounded by the network buffer pool rather than by the advertised MTU. The fix rejects frames larger than NET_ETH_MAX_FRAME_SIZE with -EMSGSIZE before any TX_DATA_PORT write, so the controller FIFO is also not left holding a command word without its payload.
items.title: Out-of-bounds write in the SMSC911x Ethernet driver when transmitting frames larger than the staging buffer

items.summary:
net_if_ipv4_addr_rm() and net_if_ipv6_addr_rm() in subsys/net/ip/net_if.c unconditionally called net_if_addr_unref() on the target address. When an earlier removal could not complete because another subsystem still held a reference (the TCP stack takes one on the local address of every connection, in tcp_conn_new() and on connect()), the address is left in place with is_added cleared and is_used still set. A second removal of such an address decremented the reference count again, consuming a reference owned by that other holder. When it was the last one, the address slot was released, its NET_EVENT_IPV*_ADDR_DEL event fired, and the slot became reusable while the holder still believed it owned a reference.

Every address lookup helper matches on is_used and not on is_added, so a half-removed address stays visible to the rest of the stack and repeat removals are readily reachable from remote input. Under IPv6 SLAAC, an on-link node that sends a Router Advertisement with a short valid lifetime causes the address to expire into the deferred state; a refreshing Router Advertisement is handled by net_if_ipv6_addr_update_lifetime(), which re-arms the lifetime timer without restoring the reference, so the next expiry performs the second, reference-stealing removal. With CONFIG_NET_IPV4_ACD and DHCPv4, repeated spoofed ARP conflicts for the device's lease drive dhcpv4_acd_event_handler() into calling net_if_ipv4_addr_rm() more than once on the same address. Where CONFIG_USERSPACE is enabled, the net_if_ipv4_addr_rm_by_index() and net_if_ipv6_addr_rm_by_index() system calls let an unprivileged user-mode thread trigger the same kernel-side release deterministically.

The impact is loss of a configured IP address while connections are still using it, and a corrupted reference count that propagates: the slot can be handed to a newly added address, and when the stale holder later tears down, net_if_addr_unref() resolves the address by value and drops the new incarnation's only reference, removing a live address a second time. The affected objects are static array slots and the counter is never decremented below zero, so there is no memory corruption or information disclosure; the consequence is denial of service against the device's network connectivity, repeatable at the attacker's pace.

The fix resolves the address before touching the reference count and returns false without calling net_if_addr_unref() when the address is already marked as removed, so the public removal API can no longer consume a reference it does not own.
items.title: Reference-count underflow in Zephyr network interface address removal releases an IP address that is still in use

items.summary: pmo-platform is a modular PMO and release-management platform for Claude Code. From 3.48 until 3.69.1, release/skills/pmo-skill-refiner/eval-viewer/generate_review.py reads untrusted model or skill output from workspace/run*/outputs/ and embeds it with json.dumps into viewer.html inside an inline script without escaping HTML metacharacters. A crafted output can close the script element and execute JavaScript when an operator generates and opens the viewer. The maintainer also confirmed that DOM-based injection through renderGrades and renderBenchmark innerHTML survives transport-only escaping, so affected render sinks must neutralize the content. Executed script can read embedded prompts and outputs, alter the viewer DOM, or modify saved feedback. This issue is fixed in version 3.69.1.
items.title: pmo-platform: Stored XSS in Eval Viewer via Unescaped JSON Embedded in Script Context

items.summary: AIT GUI provides a framework for building custom websites for real-time telemetry monitoring, commanding, and other mission operations. From 1.0.0 until 2.5.1, POST /tlm/query in ait/gui/__init__.py writes attacker-controlled field data to fields_in.txt, and its no-PCAP error path can abort before deleting that file. The unauthenticated POST /script/run route accepts a scriptPath that resolves outside ScriptRoot, reads the selected file, and executes it as Python. A network-reachable attacker can obtain the ordinary session cookie without credentials, combine the two routes, and execute arbitrary Python code with the AIT-GUI server process privileges. This issue is fixed in version 2.5.1.
items.title: AIT-GUI route chain allows unauthenticated Python execution in server process

items.summary: LinkAce is a self-hosted archive to collect website links. Prior to 2.6.0, the HTML bookmark import action in app/Actions/ImportHtmlBookmarks.php uses the global Link::whereUrl() lookup instead of restricting duplicate detection to the importing user. An authenticated user can submit a chosen URL and distinguish the skipped response count from the queued count to learn whether any account has saved that URL, including as a PRIVATE bookmark. The oracle reveals URL existence but does not directly return the bookmark contents or owner. This issue is fixed in version 2.6.0.
items.title: LinkAce: Private Bookmark URL Existence Oracle via HTML Import Skipped-Count Leaks Other Users Private Links

items.summary: LinkAce is a self-hosted archive to collect website links. Prior to 2.5.9, the authenticated GET /api/v2/lists/{list}/links endpoint in app/Http/Controllers/API/ListLinksController.php authorizes access only to the parent list and then returns its links without applying visibleForUser(). Because another user's INTERNAL or PUBLIC list may legitimately contain PRIVATE links, a normal authenticated user who may view the list can also receive those private link records, including their URLs, titles, descriptions, icons, and timestamps. Equivalent web, tag, notes, and feed handlers apply the per-link visibility scope, so this API handler is the affected exception. This issue is fixed in version 2.5.9.
items.title: LinkAce: Authenticated visibility-authorization bypass in GET /api/v2/lists/{list}/links discloses other users' private links

items.summary: Netatalk is a Free and Open Source file server suite for Unix-like operating systems. From 2.1.0 until 4.5.2, get_eacontent in libatalk/vfs/ea_ad.c subtracts MAX_REPLY_EXTRA_BYTES from a client-controlled FPGetExtAttr MaxReplySize without rejecting values from 1 through 5, and a signed-to-unsigned comparison can then select an untrusted AppleDouble ea_size. An authenticated client on a volume configured with ea = ad can use a pre-existing malformed AppleDouble sidecar to make read copy attacker-controlled bytes beyond dsi->data + 6 into the surrounding struct DSI, including protocol callback pointers. The malformed sidecar must already exist or be created through a separate local, co-export, management, restore, or vulnerability-assisted write path, and practical code execution depends on the target architecture, structure layout, and address uncertainty; runtime command execution was demonstrated on one x86-64 build. Volumes using ea = sys, ea = none, or ea = auto when it resolves to native system xattrs do not reach this path. This issue is fixed in version 4.5.2.
items.title: Netatalk: RCE - Heap out-of-bounds write in `get_eacontent()` (AppleDouble EA backend) leading to remote code execution in `afpd`

items.summary: Netatalk is a Free and Open Source file server suite for Unix-like operating systems. From 1.5.0 until 4.5.1, dsi_tcp_open in libatalk/dsi/dsi_tcp.c silently limits the bytes read from an unauthenticated DSI frame received on TCP/548 to server_quantum when the attacker-controlled dsi_len is larger, without rejecting the frame or draining the declared remainder. The same silent dsi_len truncation pattern exists in libatalk/dsi/dsi_stream.c. The leftover bytes remain queued on the TCP connection and the next dsi_stream_receive call interprets them as a new DSI header and payload, allowing a remote unauthenticated attacker to smuggle one or more additional attacker-controlled DSI frames into the same connection. This issue is fixed in version 4.5.1.
items.title: Netatalk: afpd unauthenticated DSI request smuggling via silent dsi_len truncation in dsi_tcp_open()

items.summary: Netatalk is a Free and Open Source file server suite for Unix-like operating systems. From 1.5.0 until 4.5.1, dsi_stream_receive in libatalk/dsi/dsi_stream.c independently clamps dsi_doff and dsi_len for DSIWrite requests without enforcing that the data offset is no greater than the declared frame length. An authenticated AFP client can send dsi_doff greater than dsi_len, causing the receiver to consume bytes from a queued subsequent frame before libatalk/dsi/dsi_write.c detects the inconsistency. The irreversible stream desynchronization lets the attacker control the next parsed DSI header and payload and corrupts protocol framing for the connection. This issue is fixed in version 4.5.1.
items.title: Netatalk: afpd authenticated DSIWrite request smuggling due to missing dsi_doff <= dsi_len validation

items.summary: Netatalk is a Free and Open Source file server suite for Unix-like operating systems. From 2.0.0 until 4.5.0, afp_catsearch in etc/afpd/catsearch.c computes the spec2 pointer for FPCatSearch and FPCatSearchExt from the unvalidated 16-bit spec_len request field without checking it against the remaining input length. An authenticated AFP client can cause the CatSearch handler to read stale bytes beyond the supplied request data. The bytes are used only as internal comparison criteria and are not returned to the client, and testing under standard server quantum settings did not demonstrate a crash or information disclosure. This issue is fixed in version 4.5.0.
items.title: Netatalk: Heap in-arena over-read in afpd CatSearch via unbounded spec_len in afp_catsearch()

items.summary: Netatalk is a Free and Open Source file server suite for Unix-like operating systems. Prior to 4.4.3, the afpd Spotlight RPC unmarshalling loop in etc/afpd/spotlight_marshalling.c subtracts an attacker-controlled subcount from the unsigned count variable in sl_unpack_loop without verifying that subcount is not larger. An authenticated AFP client can place an excessive element count in the sl_unpack_ints, sl_unpack_uuid, sl_unpack_floats, or sl_unpack_date handler, or in a null element, so the subtraction wraps near UINT_MAX and the loop continues reading heap memory at increasing offsets up to toc_offset, which is capped at 65000. The out-of-bounds values can be stored in dalloc structures and returned in the Spotlight RPC response, disclosing heap contents. This issue is fixed in version 4.4.3.
items.title: Netatalk: Unsigned Integer Underflow in Spotlight RPC Count Decrement (sl_unpack_loop)

items.summary: Netatalk is a Free and Open Source file server suite for Unix-like operating systems. Prior to 4.4.3, the afpd Spotlight RPC string unmarshalling path in etc/afpd/spotlight_marshalling.c uses sl_unpack_cpx to calculate slen from qlen and the attacker-controlled used_in_last_block value without preventing a negative result. An authenticated AFP client can send a complex string or UTF-16 string element that makes slen negative, and the implicit conversion to size_t causes dalloc_strndup or convert_string_allocate to read beyond the heap buffer. The out-of-bounds read can expose heap data through the RPC response or crash the worker process. This issue is fixed in version 4.4.3.
items.title: Netatalk: Integer Underflow in Spotlight RPC String Length Calculation (sl_unpack_cpx)

items.summary: wcmatch is a Python library for wildcard file-name matching. Prior to 11.2, under the default flags, matching a non-matching attacker-controlled name against an application-supplied pattern containing several star wildcards separated by literals makes the lazy .? and [^/]? segments, including _STAR and _PATH_STAR emitted by _handle_star() in wcmatch/_wcparse.py, backtrack across possible splits, so a single comparison can consume prolonged CPU time. The pattern remains a developer-controlled constant and only the name is attacker-controlled; affected paths include fnmatch.fnmatch(), glob.globmatch(), and filesystem glob scans where another user can create names, without enabling extglob or any non-default flag. This issue is fixed in 11.2.
items.title: wcmatch: Polynomial-time ReDoS when matching untrusted names against multi-star patterns (default flags)

items.summary: svglib reads SVG files and converts them to other formats. Prior to 2.3.1, the svg2rlg() renderer recursively expands nested SVG <use> references by deep-copying each referenced subtree; SvgRenderer.renderUse() in src/svglib/svglib.py calls xlink_href_target(), which rejects direct cycles but permits acyclic reference graphs with repeated fan-out. A small attacker-controlled SVG can therefore trigger exponentially increasing node expansion, consuming excessive CPU and memory in any application that renders it without a non-default option; HTML-to-PDF workflows using xhtml2pdf can reach the same renderer when an embedded data:image/svg+xml image in an HTML img element is passed to pisa.CreatePDF(). This issue is fixed in 2.3.1.
items.title: svglib: Exponential resource consumption via nested <use> references in svg2rlg

items.summary: Tapo provides Rust and Python APIs and an MCP server for TP-Link Tapo smart devices. From 0.3.1 until 0.5.0, the Streamable HTTP implementation in tapo-mcp/src/server.rs calls disable_allowed_hosts() without replacement Host or Origin validation, while TAPO_MCP_API_KEY remains optional for a listener that can bind to all interfaces. A malicious website can use DNS rebinding to send same-origin browser requests to the victim's local or LAN Tapo MCP listener when it runs without an API key. The attacker can invoke exposed tools including control_device for smart-device actuation and take_snapshot for configured cameras. Deployments with TAPO_MCP_API_KEY set are not affected by the unauthenticated path, and exploitation requires a running listener configured with real Tapo credentials and devices, plus victim interaction with the malicious site. This issue is fixed in version 0.5.0.
items.title: Tapo: DNS rebinding reaches unauthenticated Tapo MCP smart-home controls

items.summary: memtomem-stm is a short-term memory proxy gateway with proactive memory surfacing for AI agents. From 0.1.2 until 0.1.34, concurrent surfacing RPC failures can start more than one reconnect for the same dirty session because concurrent LTM recovery is not uniquely owned by a session generation. Cancellation during a post-reconnect retry can also leave the replacement transport reusable after an interrupted protocol exchange, causing session-state integrity loss or local service degradation. The duplicate-reconnect subcase was introduced in 0.1.24, while the cancellation-recovery subcase affects the broader listed range. This issue is fixed in version 0.1.34.
items.title: memtomem-stm: Concurrent LTM recovery can duplicate reconnects or reuse a cancelled transport session

items.summary:
The IPv6 Neighbor Discovery code in subsys/net/ip/ipv6_nbr.c flushes a neighbour's queued packets at the end of handle_ra_input(). The Source Link-Layer Address Option (SLLAO) is optional in a Router Advertisement; when it is absent, handle_ra_input() still obtains (or creates) a neighbour cache entry for the RA source via net_ipv6_nbr_add() with a NULL link-layer address, so the entry stays in NET_IPV6_NBR_STATE_INCOMPLETE with nbr->idx == NET_NBR_LLADDR_UNKNOWN. The pending-packet drain loop was entered unconditionally for that unresolved entry.

Each net_send_data() in the drain loop runs synchronously into net_ipv6_prepare_for_send(), which finds the neighbour still unresolved and hands the packet to net_ipv6_send_ns(), which puts it straight back onto the same pending_queue. The loop therefore never sees an empty queue. With a single queued packet it transmits a fresh Neighbor Solicitation on every iteration; with two or more queued packets it rotates the queue with no allocation and no transmission at all. The loop runs in the network RX thread with the global IPv6 neighbour mutex held.

An unauthenticated attacker on the same link can trigger this deterministically: advertise itself as a router, induce the victim to queue off-link traffic toward that router (for example by sending echo requests with an off-link source address) while leaving the solicitation unanswered, then send a second Router Advertisement without an SLLAO option. Spoofing an SLLAO-less RA from the legitimate router's link-local address has the same effect whenever traffic is queued for it. Router Advertisements are processed with no authentication whenever CONFIG_NET_IPV6_ND is enabled, which is the default for IPv6-capable builds.

The result is a permanent denial of service: the RX thread spins forever holding the neighbour lock, so all IPv6 transmission and every other user of the neighbour cache blocks, and the Neighbor Advertisement that would resolve the entry can no longer be processed. The ipv6_ns_reply_timer work item that would normally drop the pending packets also blocks on the same mutex. In the single-packet variant the loop additionally floods the link with Neighbor Solicitations. The fix restricts the flush to resolved entries (nbr->idx != NET_NBR_LLADDR_UNKNOWN), leaving the packets queued for the NS reply timeout. There is no memory-safety impact.
items.title: Infinite loop in IPv6 Router Advertisement handling when the RA omits the source link-layer address option

items.summary: Budibase is an open-source low-code platform. Prior to 3.50.0, a BASIC application user, or an unauthenticated visitor to a public write form, can store markup in a shared external datasource that a builder or administrator later evaluates in any Handlebars binding Preview that surfaces the value, including the Data-section Formula column editor or any binding drawer. jsonFormatter.format() in packages/frontend-core/src/utils/jsonFormatter.ts leaves raw strings and object keys unescaped, while packages/builder/src/components/common/bindings/EvaluationSidePanel.svelte inserts the formatted result as raw HTML. The Handlebars SafeString path preserves the attacker-controlled value, and the Builder origin lacks a Content-Security-Policy that would block the resulting script. This permits stored script execution in the higher-privileged builder or administrator session rather than the writer's own role, allowing privileged Builder API actions and workspace data access. This issue is fixed in versions 3.50.0 and 4.0.0.
items.title: Budibase: Cross-privilege Stored XSS in the Budibase Builder via broken HTML-escaping in `jsonFormatter.format()` rendered through `{@html}` in the CSP-less Builder origin

items.summary: Pydici through 2026.11.1 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows authenticated users to inject script by storing HTML in contact names rendered unescaped in the contact detail mermaid diagram. Attackers with contact edit permission can store malicious markup that Contact.relationData() interpolates and contact_detail.html renders with the safe filter, executing script in victims' sessions.
items.title: Pydici through 2026.11.1 Stored XSS via Contact Name in Relation Diagram

items.summary: LessPass self-hosted sync server backend before commit 9469b0c lacks rate limiting on the JWT login endpoints /tokens/auth/ and /auth/jwt/create/, allowing unlimited authentication attempts. Unauthenticated remote attackers can brute force passwords or perform credential stuffing against known account emails to obtain tokens granting read and write access to stored profiles.
items.title: LessPass Backend before Commit 9469b0c Missing Rate Limiting on JWT Login

items.summary: Kartones flask-calendar before commit bfde72e contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability because task_details_for_markup returns unescaped content rendered with the |safe filter. Authenticated shared calendar members can store script in task details that executes for other members, letting attackers read and modify their private calendars.
items.title: flask-calendar before commit bfde72e Stored XSS via Task Details

items.summary:
Incorrect Authorization vulnerability in phoenixframework phoenix_live_view allows an authenticated user to mount a router-mounted LiveView without the on_mount hooks of its live_session via a phx_join message that carries neither a "url" nor a "redirect" key.

The catch-all clause of the private Phoenix.LiveView.Channel.authorize_session/3 in lib/phoenix_live_view/channel.ex accepts a join without a URL for any session, including a root LiveView mounted at the router. The channel then mounts the LiveView with no route, and only a route adds the live_session hooks to the mount lifecycle. Checks that those hooks perform on the connected mount do not run, and event checks that they attach through attach_hook/4 are never attached. The attacker needs a valid session token for the LiveView, which only the HTTP render issues, after the hooks pass there. on_mount hooks declared in the LiveView module still run.

This issue affects phoenix_live_view: from 0.16.0 before 1.0.20, from 1.1.0-rc.0 before 1.1.34, and from 1.2.0-rc.0 before 1.2.14.
items.title: Joining a LiveView without `"url"` skips its `live_session` `on_mount` hooks

items.summary:
flowintel contains an authorization flaw in its user deletion functionality. Organization-scoped administrators (org admins) are able to delete platform-level administrator accounts through both the browser-based admin interface and the REST API.

The existing authorization logic verified that an org admin could only target users within their own organization, but it did not enforce the privilege hierarchy between organization admins and platform admins. As a result, an authenticated org admin could issue a deletion request against any platform-admin account belonging to the same organization, causing the target account, its sessions, and related records to be permanently removed.

Impact:
- Loss of platform-level administrative oversight
- Potential disruption of platform-wide management functions
- Removal of higher-privilege accounts that should be protected from lower-privilege roles

Affected versions: flowintel prior to 4.1.0
items.title: flowintel: Organization Admin Can Delete Platform Admin Accounts Due to Missing Privilege Hierarchy Check

items.summary: Penpot 2.18.0 before 2.18.2 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows authenticated users with edit rights to bypass the sanitize-svg-element blocklist using namespace-prefixed SVG elements. Attackers can upload SVGs containing elements like x:script or attributes like x:onload, which are served inline as image/svg+xml to run JavaScript in victims' Penpot sessions.
items.title: Penpot 2.18.0 before 2.18.2 Stored XSS via Namespace-Prefixed SVG Elements

items.summary:
flowintel contains multiple related flaws that allow an authenticated attacker to inject arbitrary HTML or script into pages viewed by other users.

- Timeline rendering: the timeline library's autolinking feature rewrote already-sanitised case notes and imported MISP attribute values into generated HTML link elements. Crafted text containing quote characters could break out of the generated attribute context, altering the surrounding markup and enabling script execution in the victim's browser.

- Search highlighting: the highlight injection logic used a regular expression to locate text between angle brackets and spliced <mark> elements into the resulting string. Because the pattern could match inside HTML attribute values, the rewrite could corrupt or inject content into attributes of already-sanitised markup, again leading to DOM-based cross-site scripting.

- Content-Type confusion: three analyser selection endpoints returned session-stored JSON strings with a text/html content type. A browser receiving such a response will parse and render the body as HTML, so any HTML or script embedded in the stored value is executed in the victim's context.

Preconditions: the attacker must be an authenticated user with the ability to create or import case content (notes, MISP attributes) containing specially crafted quote or angle-bracket sequences. The victim must subsequently open the affected case timeline, run a search, or request one of the selection endpoints.

Impact: successful exploitation yields DOM-based cross-site scripting in the victim's browser session, potentially allowing disclosure of case data, session manipulation, or execution of arbitrary actions under the victim's identity.

Affected versions: flowintel prior to 4.1.0.
items.title: flowintel DOM-based XSS via Timeline Autolinking, Search Highlighting, and Content-Type Confusion

items.summary:
flowintel contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows authenticated non-administrative users to access sensitive configuration data and logs intended for administrators only.

The notification page and alert API responses exposed sensitive fields, including webhook URLs, signing secrets, IMAP credentials, and delivery logs, in the initial data or JSON responses. Although the user interface hid the configuration form from non-admin users, the underlying data remained accessible via the page source or API endpoints. This exposure included historical webhook URLs that may contain active bearer tokens.

An attacker with a valid non-admin account could retrieve these credentials and logs, potentially leading to unauthorized access to notification services, impersonation of the application in webhook deliveries, or further lateral movement within the infrastructure.

Affected versions: flowintel < 4.1.0
items.title: flowintel Information Disclosure of Webhook Secrets and Logs to Non-Admin Users

items.summary:
flowintel contains an Insecure Direct Object Reference (IDOR) vulnerability affecting multiple endpoints that manage child records of cases and tasks. An authenticated user with access to one case or task could read or modify records belonging to other cases by supplying identifiers of those records directly in the request.

Affected operations include:
- Reading task notes, subtasks, and URL tools by referencing their IDs without verifying they belong to the authorized task
- Retrieving task assignees for a task belonging to a different case
- Editing or deleting timeline events and timeline event links belonging to another case
- Editing or removing case connectors belonging to another case
- Invoking connector module operations (MISP, generic connectors, worker calls) by combining an authorized case with a connector link from a different case

The root cause is that the application authorized the parent resource (case or task) in the URL but then fetched or operated on the child record independently without verifying the child's ownership relationship to the authorized parent.

Security impact: an authenticated user can exfiltrate sensitive threat intelligence data from cases they do not have access to, and can modify or delete timeline entries, connector configurations, and other records in unauthorized cases, leading to data integrity loss and potential disruption of incident response workflows.

Affected versions: flowintel prior to 4.1.0
items.title: flowintel Insecure Direct Object Reference Allows Cross-Case Data Access and Modification

items.summary:
FlowIntel contained a Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF) vulnerability affecting fourteen web routes that performed destructive or state-changing operations. The affected routes accepted HTTP GET requests in addition to (or instead of) POST, which bypassed the Flask-WTF CSRF token validation that is only enforced on non-GET requests.

The vulnerable operations included:
- Case deletion and case merging
- Organisation removal from a case
- Task deletion (case and template)
- Case template and note template deletion
- Connector, connector instance, and icon deletion
- Custom tag deletion and status change
- Taxonomy and galaxy status changes

An attacker who could induce an authenticated user to follow a crafted link or load a page containing a cross-site navigation (e.g., an image tag or redirect) could trigger any of these destructive actions using the victim's session cookie, without the victim's explicit consent or awareness. No special privileges beyond a valid authenticated session with the appropriate role (editor or admin) were required on the victim's account.

Security impact: unauthorized deletion or modification of cases, tasks, templates, connectors, icons, custom tags, taxonomies, and galaxies belonging to the victim or the organisation, resulting in loss of data integrity.

Affected versions: FlowIntel prior to 4.1.0
items.title: FlowIntel CSRF via GET-accepted destructive web routes bypassing Flask-WTF protection

items.summary:
Flowintel disabled TLS certificate verification for all MISP API connections and used unverified SSL contexts for IMAP and SMTP STARTTLS mail connections. This allowed an on-path (man-in-the-middle) attacker positioned between Flowintel and its MISP or mail servers to impersonate the remote server and intercept sensitive data.

Affected connections include:
- All MISP HTTPS API calls (event retrieval, attribute search, event creation, connectivity checks, and API validation)
- SMTP STARTTLS connections used for sending email notifications
- IMAP TLS connections used for fetching mail archives and testing connectivity

An attacker who can observe or intercept network traffic between Flowintel and the MISP or mail server could:
- Capture MISP API keys and mail credentials (SMTP/IMAP passwords)
- Read all threat intelligence data exchanged (events, attributes, objects, reports)
- Inject or modify threat intelligence data returned to Flowintel

The vulnerability required no authentication on the part of the attacker and no user interaction; it was exploitable by any party with a network position between Flowintel and its configured MISP or mail endpoints.

Affected versions: Flowintel prior to 4.1.0.
items.title: Flowintel Disables TLS Certificate Verification for MISP and Mail Connections

items.summary: The My Calendar – Accessible Event Manager plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'event_street' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 3.8.13 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Exploitation requires that an administrator has granted the mc_add_events capability to Subscriber-level users via the plugin's Permissions settings; once granted, the Subscriber can store the payload without the mc_edit_locations capability because mc_admin_save() does not enforce it before calling mc_insert_location().
items.title: My Calendar <= 3.8.13 - Authenticated (Subscriber+) Stored Cross-Site Scripting via 'event_street' Address Field

items.summary:
FlowIntel contains multiple security flaws in its note variable resolution, chatbot API tooling, and AI report generation.

- Note variable references (e.g. cross-case or cross-task lookups) were resolved using the viewing user's privileges rather than the destination case's audience. An authenticated user with access to a shared or imported note could embed references to private cases, causing sensitive case data to be pulled into AI report requests, exports, and MISP sends without the referenced case's audience having granted read access.

- The chatbot API tool permitted the language model to invoke any FlowIntel API endpoint, including administrative routes and state-changing GET operations, without an allow-list or path validation. An attacker who can influence the model's instructions (e.g. via untrusted case content) could induce data modification or access restricted endpoints.

- AI report generation passed the Ollama bearer token and full case content as command-line arguments to a child process, exposing them in the system process table to any local user.

Affected versions: FlowIntel prior to 4.1.0.
items.title: FlowIntel Insecure Note Variable Resolution, Over-Permissive Chatbot API Access, and Credential Exposure in Process Arguments

items.summary:
The flowintel Docker build workflow used the GitHub Actions checkout action with default credential persistence, causing the job authentication token to be written into the repository's Git configuration file. This file became part of the Docker build context and could be retained in exported build cache layers, even though Git metadata was stripped from the final runtime image.

An attacker with access to the CI/CD build cache or build environment could extract the persisted token and use it to gain unauthorized access to the private source repository.

Impact:
- Exposure of a valid authentication token to the private repository
- Potential unauthorized read access to source code and repository metadata

Affected versions: flowintel < 4.1.0
items.title: flowintel CI/CD Workflow Exposes Checkout Credentials in Docker Build Cache

items.summary:
flowintel contains a log injection vulnerability in its case history (audit log) subsystem. The case history is stored as a line-delimited file where each line represents a single event attributed to a specific user. User-controlled fields, including user names, event messages, and case titles used during case merging, were written to the history file without sanitizing embedded line separator characters (such as carriage return, line feed, vertical tab, form feed, and Unicode line/paragraph separators).

An authenticated user with the ability to create or modify case history entries could embed line separators in these fields. Upon writing, the injected separators would split a single intended entry into multiple lines, each of which the history format interprets as a distinct event. This allows an attacker to forge additional history entries attributed to arbitrary users, corrupting the audit trail and undermining the integrity of case records.

The vulnerability affects the case history append and merge operations. No authentication bypass or privilege escalation is required beyond normal case-management access.

Affected versions: flowintel prior to 4.1.0.
items.title: flowintel Case History Log Injection via Line Separator Characters in User-Authored Fields

items.summary:
FlowIntel contains a resource exhaustion vulnerability in its file-to-note conversion feature. When a user converts an attached CSV or JSON file into a case note, the application renders the data as a Markdown table by padding every row to the maximum column count. A crafted file with a small number of filled cells but a very large number of columns (or keys) causes the application to allocate a quadratic number of padded table cells, potentially exhausting a worker process in memory or CPU.

The same issue affects nested JSON values rendered inside table cells, where pretty-printed indentation further inflates the output size.

Preconditions:
- An authenticated user with access to a case in FlowIntel
- Ability to attach and convert a CSV or JSON file to a note

Impact:
- Denial of service: exhaustion of a worker process, potentially disrupting service for other users
- No confidentiality or integrity impact

Affected versions: FlowIntel prior to 4.1.0
items.title: FlowIntel: Resource Exhaustion via Sparse CSV/JSON Table Expansion During File-to-Note Conversion

items.summary: Improper neutralization of special elements in data query logic (Cypher injection) in the orderBy placeholder handling for custom queries in Neo4j Spring Data Neo4j versions 6.1.0 through 8.0.8 and 8.1.0 through 8.1.2 allows a remote attacker to read database contents via blind reads, write read content into new nodes, or, if APOC and APOC file export are enabled, to write query results to a file in the database's accessible file system via crafted sort order parameters. Exploitation requires an application that passes unvalidated user input as the orderBy value to a custom Cypher query using the placeholder directive.
items.title: Cypher injection via orderBy placeholder in Spring Data Neo4j custom queries

items.summary:
In the nrfconnect/ncs-zigbee repository, the GitHub Actions workflow
.github/workflows/build_documentation.yml used the pull_request_target trigger
while checking out and executing untrusted pull request code. This allowed a
pull request from a fork to run attacker-controlled code in the base repository
context with a write-scoped GITHUB_TOKEN (contents: write, pages: write,
pull-requests: write), enabling remote code execution in CI, token
exfiltration, and unauthorized modification of repository content and GitHub
Pages. The workflow was disabled and then rewritten to remove the issue.
items.title: GitHub Actions pull_request_target code injection in nrfconnect/ncs-zigbee (build_documentation.yml)

items.summary: The FV Flowplayer Video Player plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'comment' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 7.5.57.7212 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. This requires the plugin's 'Parse Vimeo and YouTube links' setting to be enabled, which wires do_shortcode into the comment_text filter chain and allows the [fvplayer] shortcode to be rendered from comment content.
items.title: FV Flowplayer Video Player <= 7.5.57.7212 - Unauthenticated Stored Cross-Site Scripting via 'caption' Shortcode Attribute

items.summary: The FV Flowplayer Video Player plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'data[videos][0][fv_wp_flowplayer_field_src]' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 7.5.57.7212 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. The fv_player_db_save AJAX endpoint's INSERT path is gated only by a per-user preview nonce and never calls current_user_can(), allowing any authenticated subscriber-level user who possesses their own nonce to store the malicious payload. Exploitation by attackers with subscriber-level access and above requires that administrator has enabled the plugin option fvwpflowplayer['profile_videos_enable_bio']=true (off by default), which enqueues the shortcode editor and the per-user preview_nonce on wp-admin/profile.php for every logged-in user. On a default installation, where that is not configured, the vulnerability requires attackers with contributor-level access and above.
items.title: FV Flowplayer Video Player <= 7.5.57.7212 - Authenticated (Subscriber+) Stored Cross-Site Scripting via 'fv_wp_flowplayer_field_src' Parameter

items.summary:
Flowintel's template repository subsystem did not adequately constrain file access to the configured repository base directory. Two related weaknesses existed:

- Repository registration and editing accepted arbitrary local paths without verifying they resolved inside the configured REPOSITORY_BASE_PATH, allowing an authenticated user to point a repository at any readable directory on the host.
- Manifest and template file lookups used normalized (non-canonical) path joins and a startswith-based guard that could be bypassed by symbolic links, permitting reads of files outside the intended repository.

An authenticated user with the ability to add or edit a template repository could therefore cause the application to read and return the contents of arbitrary files readable by the service account, including configuration files, credentials, or other sensitive data.

Affected: Flowintel versions prior to 4.1.0.
items.title: Flowintel Template Repository Path Traversal and Symlink Escape Allows Arbitrary File Read

items.summary: A vulnerability has been identified in webauthn-kotlin versions 1.1.0 through 1.1.3, where an exported device-credential authentication activity launches attacker-supplied intents without validation, potentially allowing a malicious application on the same Android device to access application-protected data, depending on the host application’s content-provider configuration.
items.title: CVE-2026-133615

items.summary:
Flowintel's community data launcher script passes the admin API key as a command-line argument to a child Python helper process. On Unix-like systems, process arguments are readable by all local users via standard tools such as ps or by reading /proc/<pid>/cmdline, allowing any local user to observe the key while the helper process is running.

An attacker with local access to the host can capture the admin API key during the brief window in which the helper process is active. Possession of the key grants full administrative access to the Flowintel REST API, enabling unauthorized creation, modification, or deletion of threat intelligence data, users, roles, and organisations.

Preconditions:
- The victim must invoke the community data import or deletion command (launch.sh -tdc or -dtdc) with the API key supplied as a positional argument.
- The attacker must have a local user account on the same host and be able to observe process listings during the helper execution window.

Impact:
- Disclosure of the Flowintel admin API key to any local user.
- Subsequent full administrative control over the Flowintel instance via its REST API.

Affected: <4.1.0
items.title: Flowintel Community Data Launcher Exposes Admin API Key in Child Process Arguments

items.summary: FFmpeg 7.0 through 9.0.2 contains an out-of-bounds read vulnerability in dvdvideo_menu_next_ps_block() in libavformat/dvdvideodec.c when demuxing DVD menu domains. Attackers can craft a DVD image whose last cell sector and NAV next-VOBU pointer bypass the end-of-cell check, overreading pgc->cell_playback and crashing the process.
items.title: FFmpeg 7.0 through 9.0.2 Out-of-Bounds Read via dvdvideo_menu_next_ps_block()

items.summary:
Convert::ASN1 versions before 0.37 for Perl allow memory exhaustion via a declared element length passed unchecked to sysread in asn_read and asn_get.

The length an element declares in its BER header is passed to sysread as the read size. Perl grows the target buffer to that size before reading, so memory is allocated from the declared length, not from the data received. A 6-byte header can declare a length of up to 4GB.

A single header makes the reading process allocate the declared size. Where the allocation fails, perl exits with "Out of memory", which eval cannot catch.
items.title: Convert::ASN1 versions before 0.37 for Perl allow memory exhaustion via a declared element length passed unchecked to sysread in asn_read and asn_get

items.summary:
Convert::ASN1 versions before 0.37 for Perl allow CPU exhaustion via unbounded arc length in OBJECT IDENTIFIER decoding and encoding.

The content of an OBJECT IDENTIFIER or RELATIVE-OID element is passed to unpack "w*" on decode, and the arcs of an OID string to pack "w*" on encode. Perl converts each arc to or from its decimal string in time quadratic in the arc's length, and nothing limits that length.

An attacker who controls the decoded data, or an OID string passed to encode, can exhaust CPU with a single oversized arc.
items.title: Convert::ASN1 versions before 0.37 for Perl allow CPU exhaustion via unbounded arc length in OBJECT IDENTIFIER decoding and encoding

items.summary:
Convert::ASN1 versions before 0.37 for Perl allow memory exhaustion via unlimited recursion depth in constructed-form string decoding.

Any constructed-form string element causes the decoder to recurse on the element's contents. The BER encoding controls nesting depth at four bytes per level, with no bound checked. Perl recursion is heap-allocated, so the process grows without a stack crash.

An attacker who controls the decoded data can exhaust memory with a small deeply nested constructed string.
items.title: Convert::ASN1 versions before 0.37 for Perl allow memory exhaustion via unlimited recursion depth in constructed-form string decoding

items.summary:
Convert::ASN1 versions before 0.37 for Perl allow memory exhaustion via zero-length BIT STRING content.

A BIT STRING with zero content octets passes -1 to substr as the length. Perl reads a negative length as an offset from the end of the string, so the decoded value is nearly all of the input that follows the element. In the constructed form each zero-length segment copies the rest of the input again, so memory grows with the square of the input size.

An attacker who controls the decoded data can exhaust memory with a short constructed BIT STRING. The resulting value also contains bytes from adjacent input.
items.title: Convert::ASN1 versions before 0.37 for Perl allow memory exhaustion via zero-length BIT STRING content

items.summary:
Convert::ASN1 versions before 0.37 for Perl allow CPU exhaustion via exponent-notation string in INTEGER encoding.

The encoder routes any value with abs >= 2**31 to i2osp without validating that it is an integer. A string in exponent notation such as "1e8000" passes that threshold. Math::BigInt expands it to an 8001-digit integer, and i2osp's per-octet conversion loop is quadratic in that size.

An attacker who controls encoded INTEGER values can exhaust CPU with a short exponent-notation string.
items.title: Convert::ASN1 versions before 0.37 for Perl allow CPU exhaustion via exponent-notation string in INTEGER encoding

items.summary:
Convert::ASN1 versions before 0.37 for Perl allow CPU exhaustion via unchecked exponent length in binary REAL decoding.

Binary REAL decoding never bounds-checks the exponent length against the available content. For a minimal one-byte binary REAL, the exponent byte is read from outside the element, making the mantissa length -1. Perl reads a negative length as an offset from the end of the string, so the mantissa is nearly all of the input that follows the element. The long-form exponent path also omits the extra length octet when sizing the mantissa.

An attacker who controls the decoded data can exhaust CPU with a list of such values, as each mantissa loop iterates over the remaining input. The decoded values are also computed from bytes outside each element.
items.title: Convert::ASN1 versions before 0.37 for Perl allow CPU exhaustion via unchecked exponent length in binary REAL decoding

items.summary:
Convert::ASN1 versions before 0.37 for Perl allow memory exhaustion via unbounded MSG_PEEK buffer doubling in asn_recv.

asn_recv peeks the socket in a loop, doubling the buffer size on each pass until a tag and length can be decoded. An inverted boolean guard ($tb || rather than $tb &&) prevents the need-more-data exit from firing once a tag byte has been decoded. When asn_decode_length returns no value because the length is absent or incomplete, no exit fires for that case either. MSG_PEEK leaves socket data unconsumed, so each re-peek returns at once while the buffer size doubles.

A single truncated BER header sent to a process calling asn_recv doubles the peek buffer until memory is exhausted. Perl's realloc failure is fatal and not catchable with eval.
items.title: Convert::ASN1 versions before 0.37 for Perl allow memory exhaustion via unbounded MSG_PEEK buffer doubling in asn_recv

items.summary:
Convert::ASN1 versions before 0.37 for Perl allow CPU exhaustion via quadratic bigint loop in os2ip.

Every INTEGER or ENUMERATED longer than four content octets reaches os2ip, which iterates over each content octet with $result = ($result * 256) + $octet. Each multiplication operates on a bigint that grows by one octet per step, so decoding an n-octet value takes O(n^2) bigint work. Nothing limits content length before this loop runs.

An attacker who controls the decoded data can exhaust CPU with a single oversized INTEGER or ENUMERATED value.
items.title: Convert::ASN1 versions before 0.37 for Perl allow CPU exhaustion via quadratic bigint loop in os2ip

items.summary: Flyto2 Core is an execution kernel for automation and AI-agent workflows. Prior to 2.26.8, the MCP run_recipe tool in src/core/mcp_handler.py accepts a caller-controlled recipe_name that load_recipe() in src/cli/recipe.py appends to the src/recipes path without resolved-path containment. Parent-directory segments can therefore make Flyto load and execute a YAML workflow outside the bundled recipe directory, bypassing the boundary represented by list_recipes(). This does not necessarily provide unrestricted code execution because available workflow modules remain subject to Flyto's module policy, but it permits unintended execution of allowed browser, network, file, and data-processing modules. This issue is fixed in version 2.26.8.
items.title: Flyto2 Core: Path traversal in MCP `run_recipe` allows execution of workflows outside bundled recipe directory

items.summary: Aether Project AMF supports termination of NAS signalling, NAS ciphering & integrity protection, registration management, connection management, mobility management, access authentication and authorization, security context management. Prior to 3.1.6, a malformed NGAP PathSwitchRequest can contain a UESecurityCapabilities information element whose extensible APER bit-string representation has no bytes even though decoding reports no error. In ngap/handler.go, HandlePathSwitchRequest checks only whether the element is present before six index-zero reads of its encryption and integrity algorithm fields, causing an unrecovered panic in the NGAP receive goroutine and terminating the AMF. The described attacker is a rogue or compromised gNB on the N2 interface and additionally needs a registered UE's AMF-UE-NGAP-ID; a bare over-the-air UE cannot trigger the issue. This issue is fixed in version 3.1.6.
items.title: Aether Project amf: panic on an unrecovered NGAP goroutine

items.summary: Poweradmin is a web-based DNS administration tool for PowerDNS server. From 4.0.0 until 4.2.6, 4.3.5, and 4.4.1, lib/Domain/Service/MfaService.php verifies email second-factor codes through MfaService::verifyCode() without limiting failed attempts, and lib/Application/Controller/MfaVerifyController.php logs failures without throttling them. An attacker who knows the user's password can repeatedly guess the six-digit code during its ten-minute validity period when email MFA is enabled, potentially bypassing the second factor; the advisory notes MFA is disabled by default and that the practical request rate was not measured. This issue is fixed in versions 4.2.6, 4.3.5, and 4.4.1.

items.summary: RepoManager is a self-hosted deb/rpm package repository. Prior to 5.13.3, a registered host or a party with its host/API credential can submit package metadata. Inventory reporting accepts package name and version, while available-update reporting accepts package name, version, and repository; the repository field exists only on that path. RepoManager stores these values, and stored values are rendered on the host's package detail page without preventing stored HTML or JavaScript from executing. An administrator must later view the page for script execution. The script runs in the administrator's authenticated browser session and can expose administrative data or forge privileged requests; the advisory describes possible escalation through admin-only functionality. Fixed in 5.13.3.
items.title: RepoManager: Stored XSS via host-reported package metadata

items.summary: NLTK (Natural Language Toolkit) is a suite of open source Python modules, data sets, and tutorials supporting research and development in Natural Language Processing. Prior to 3.10.4, WordNet Synset.tree and acyclic_tree traverse relation graphs through recursive utility helpers without a depth bound. Exploitation requires the host application to load an attacker-influenced custom or foreign WordNet-format lexical resource; no relation in NLTK's bundled WordNet 3.0 corpus reaches the crash threshold. An excessively deep relation graph in such a resource can exceed the Python recursion limit and terminate the traversal or request worker. This issue is fixed in version 3.10.4.
items.title: Natural Language Toolkit (NLTK): Uncontrolled recursion (crash DoS) in Synset.tree()/acyclic_tree() via WordNet relation traversal

items.summary: NLTK (Natural Language Toolkit) is a suite of open source Python modules, data sets, and tutorials supporting research and development in Natural Language Processing. From 3.6 to 3.10.3, XMLCorpusView._read_xml_fragment accumulates 1 KiB blocks and repeatedly applies whole-buffer XML validation while a comment or CDATA terminator remains ahead. A large comment in an attacker-controlled corpus file causes quadratic CPU consumption through documented XML corpus readers across the affected range. On 3.6 and 3.9.2, a large CDATA section incurs the quadratic scan before rejection, while on 3.10.3 both comment and CDATA documents are read successfully. This vulnerability is fixed in 3.10.4.
items.title: NLTK: XMLCorpusView comment and CDATA parsing permits quadratic CPU denial of service

items.summary: NLTK (Natural Language Toolkit) is a suite of open source Python modules, data sets, and tutorials supporting research and development in Natural Language Processing. From 3.10.0 until 3.10.4, TokenSearcher.findall and Text.findall accept caller-controlled regular expressions with an unbounded number of capturing groups throughout the affected range. Starting in 3.10.3, nltk.redos.compile and RegexpTokenizer expose the same compile-time vector. The third-party regex engine compiles group-dense patterns with roughly quadratic cost before the match-time timeout begins, allowing a small unauthenticated request to exhaust CPU and deny service. This issue is fixed in version 3.10.4.
items.title: NLTK: Compile-time regex DoS in NLTK search/tokenizer sinks: quadratic regex-engine compile bypasses the match-only timeout

items.summary: NLTK (Natural Language Toolkit) is a suite of open source Python modules, data sets, and tutorials supporting research and development in Natural Language Processing. Prior to 3.10.4, SeekableUnicodeStreamReader.readline appends each new block to a growing character buffer and reruns splitlines over the entire buffer on every iteration. An attacker-controlled corpus file containing one very long unterminated line therefore causes quadratic CPU consumption in line-oriented corpus readers and can deny service. This issue is fixed in version 3.10.4.
items.title: NLTK: Quadratic-time DoS in SeekableUnicodeStreamReader.readline on an unterminated corpus line via per-iteration full-buffer rescan

items.summary: NLTK (Natural Language Toolkit) is a suite of open source Python modules, data sets, and tutorials supporting research and development in Natural Language Processing. Prior to 3.10.4, XMLCorpusView.read_block rebuilds the full root-to-node context path with "/".join(context) for every start tag while searching for a matching element. Deeply nested attacker-influenced corpus XML therefore causes quadratic pure-Python work and can pin a processing worker, resulting in denial of service. This issue is fixed in version 3.10.4.
items.title: NLTK: Quadratic CPU exhaustion in NLTK XMLCorpusView.read_block via deeply nested XML corpus tags

items.summary: Git LFS is a Git extension for versioning large files. From 0.6.0 until 3.8.1, Git LFS reads Git configuration options defined for a submodule without checking certain values for embedded line-ending control characters. A malicious repository can insert control characters such as line feed (LF) into those values to mimic options that cause Git LFS to execute an attacker-controlled command or binary while fetching or adding objects. This issue is fixed in version 3.8.1.
items.title: Git LFS may execute arbitrary commands via crafted Git configurations

items.summary: django-docutils provides reStructuredText support for Django. Prior to 0.30.0, public rendering paths including publish_doctree, publish_html_from_source, publish_html_from_doctree, publish_parts_from_doctree, the {% rst %} template tag, the rst template filter, DocutilsTemplates, and DocutilsView pass lower-trust reStructuredText to Docutils without disabling file_insertion_enabled, raw_enabled, ambient docutils.conf processing, or unsafe URI schemes and without consistently sanitizing doctrees. An attacker who can influence rendered reStructuredText can use include or csv-table directives to read local files or cause server-side URL requests, or use raw HTML and unsafe URI output to inject stored script-capable content. Applications that render only trusted static reStructuredText are not affected unless attackers can influence it. This issue is fixed in version 0.30.0.
items.title: django-docutils unsafe Docutils defaults allow local file disclosure, SSRF, and stored XSS

items.summary: ClassiCube before 1.4.0 contains a heap-based out-of-bounds write vulnerability in Png_Decode in src/Bitmap.c that allows malicious servers to corrupt client memory by sending a PNG with a duplicate IHDR chunk. Attackers can supply crafted PNGs via texture pack URLs or player skins so the unreset bufferIdx underflows remaining space, letting IDAT data overflow the buffer to crash clients or execute code.
items.title: ClassiCube before 1.4.0 Heap Out-of-Bounds Write via Png_Decode Duplicate IHDR

items.summary: Chamilo LMS 1.11.10 before 1.11.16 contains an unauthenticated SQL injection vulnerability in the searchOptionsFromTags function through the options parameter of extra_field.ajax.php. Attackers can send POST requests with a malicious JSON options array to inject SQL into the IN clause and extract database information. Attackers can supply crafted URLs that the ImageHunter component fetches through url.openConnection() to reach internal services and bypass network restrictions. items.title: CVE-2018-25442

items.summary: Reddit Top RSS through commit 5e38bfd contains a reflected cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to inject scripts through the unescaped score GET parameter. Attackers can craft links with a score value that closes the input value attribute in html.php, executing JavaScript in victims' browsers. items.title: Reddit Top RSS Reflected XSS via score Parameter in html.php

Attackers can send crafted GET requests to index.php?r=editorLink, where EditorLinkController concatenates url and route unvalidated, redirecting victims to attacker-controlled sites for phishing. items.title: LimeSurvey 6.5.0 < 6.16.11 Open Redirect via editorLink url Parameter
